answer.summary: Jessica Hische keeps branding exploration flexible by separating the eventual rights buyout from the creative rounds, then scales her involvement to the client’s needs and budget. She says her projects typically run $25,000–$35,000, with lower-cost consulting possible depending on how she is brought in.

sections.heading: Separate creative work from the final buyout
sections.content: Unlike the common approach she describes—billing each round as work-for-hire and building buyout rights into every round, making each round more expensive—Hische treats branding more like commercial lettering. The process stays lighter and less expensive while exploring; the client pays to own the selected final work, rather than every rejected option. That leaves room to explore and limits sunk costs if stakeholders change direction or the project must restart.

sections.heading: Scale the engagement to the client
sections.content: She varies her approach based on the client’s goals, needs, and budget: she might join early alongside an internal team or external agency, or consult at the end after a company has developed the work most of the way internally. She also emphasizes collaborating with in-house designers and making them feel invested, rather than taking over their work.

sections.heading: Typical price range
sections.content: Hische says most of her projects end up around $25,000–$35,000, while the cost can be lower if she is brought in only as a consultant. She contrasts this with branding people telling her that this kind of work should cost at least $60,000–$70,000; she frames her flexible pricing as a way to fit different needs, not as a fixed price or guarantee.
